messages:
sasha_support: FYI — AcmePayments opened a P1 about sudden p99 spikes + some 502s after the model rollout this morning. They report timeouts ~8-12s and a few dropped requests. ticket: INC-4521 from support-bot pasted below :rotating_light:

support-bot: [INC-4521] Customer: AcmePayments — p99 latency up 4x since 09:12 UTC, started after model=v3.2.1 rollout; they see occasional 502/504. Attached logs show GPU OOMs then long tails.

sasha_support: Paste of customer logs they sent: ```2026-03-17T09:14:22Z ERROR serve: request 0x7f9f: allocation failed: cuda out of memory
2026-03-17T09:14:22Z WARN runtime: fallback to CPU path (slow) for request 0x7f9f
2026-03-17T09:14:25Z INFO router: queued 12ms, run 2814ms, send 24ms
```

jun_ops: oncall checking now. which fleet/region?

sasha_support: eu-west-1, fleet-gpu-a (pools: gpu-a1,gpu-a2). Affected customer route: /v1/generate?customer=acme-pay.

kevin_oncall: seeing corresponding spikes in p99 on dashboards starting 09:11 UTC. GPU memory pressure metric (gpu_mem_frag_ratio) jumps from ~0.12 to 0.78 on node gpu-a2-12 around that time. Also saw a spike in KV cache size for that customer route. :eyes:

maria_dev: interesting — KV cache growth + fragmentation suggests per-request KV entries aren't getting evicted. any recent change in model or tokenizer that could increase KV size?

aj_chan: model v3.2.1 introduced dynamic prompt expansion for system messages (longer context) + a slight change in kv encoding. we added a small header per request that can increase kv length by ~40-80 bytes. shouldn't cause OOM alone though.

jun_ops: grabbed pod logs and dmesg. pattern: memory fragmentation -> sporadic OOM -> runtime falls back to CPU -> long tail. Pod: gpu-serve-12. Logs: ```Mar 17 09:13:54 gpu-serve-12 cuda: allocation 0x7f... failed, free 512MB, requested 1.2GB
Mar 17 09:13:55 gpu-serve-12 runtime: kv_cache_size=1.4GB (per-customer), kv_entries=124k
Mar 17 09:13:55 gpu-serve-12 runtime: mem_frag_ratio=0.79, allocator=dlmalloc, arenas=8
```

kevin_oncall: dlmalloc arenas=8 + MALLOC_ARENA_MAX not set could be causing host-side fragmentation that cascades into GPU allocations (we've seen this). Also qemu stats show many small allocations due to tokenization changes.

maria_dev: steps to repro locally? can we simulate customer load with new model and long system prompts to see if KV growth matches?

aj_chan: created a short repro script that sends 30 concurrent sessions with ~2k token system prompts. will run against a staging gpu instance and dump kv metrics.

infra-bot: created incident ticket INC-4521 and linked runbook runbook/gpu-oom. Assigned to jun_ops and kevin_oncall.

jun_ops: mitigation idea: 1) rollback model v3.2.1 for acme route to v3.2.0 (quick rollback) 2) temporarily disable prefix caching for that route so KV doesn't accumulate 3) reduce batch size and max tokens for that customer 4) restart gpu-serve-12 to defragment allocator as short-term. anyone opposed?

sasha_support: AcmeOps asked for low-impact mitigation first; they prefer toggling server-side options vs model rollback.

kevin_oncall: agree with staged approach. I'll patch route config: set cache.enabled=false for acme-pay, set max_batch_tokens=1024 for that route and apply a soft RPS throttle (80%) to reduce peak concurrent KV creations. Also schedule a rolling restart for that node in 10m window.

maria_dev: on the runtime side, we should enable eager KV eviction when per-customer kv_size > 1GB (threshold). quick patch we can hotfix?

aj_chan: can push kv-evict hotfix to staging now. but need a canary plan. we should monitor p95/p99 and KV size.

jun_ops: executed route patch at 09:21 UTC. support-bot notified customer. initiating rolling restart on gpu-a2-12 now.

support-bot: Notified AcmePayments: "We've applied temporary routing changes and are restarting the node. We'll follow up with more details." :white_check_mark:

kevin_oncall: post-patch metrics: p99 for route dropped from 9.8s to 1.4s within 90s. KV size decreased from 1.4GB to ~420MB after eviction. No further OOMs observed on that node. :thumbsup:

maria_dev: nice. follow-ups: 1) permanent fix: allocator tuning (set MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=1 in GPU service env) + upgrade allocator to tcmalloc for lower fragmentation 2) add KV eviction policy and per-model kv size limits 3) add alerting on per-customer kv growth (alert at 800MB) 4) update model onboarding checklist to include KV size perf test for tokenization changes.

aj_chan: agreed. I'll open a PR for kv eviction policy + add regression test to perf harness.

jun_ops: creating ops ticket to set MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=1 on fleet-gpu-a and schedule controlled rollout. ops-ticket: OPS-7782.

kevin_oncall: closing INC-4521 for now as mitigations held and customer confirmed lower latencies. keeping incident open for postmortem.

sasha_support: Acme confirmed lower latencies and asked for a writeup. I'll draft a customer-facing summary once we have the postmortem notes.

maria_dev: adding to backlog: runtime-evict, allocator-migration, onboarding-tests. tagging @aj_chan on PRs.

aj_chan: running staging repro now; will post results in 10-15m.

infra-bot: Incident INC-4521 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Postmortem required within 72h.

kevin_oncall: thanks everyone. main takeaway: tokenizer change increased kv footprint + host allocator fragmentation amplified GPU OOMs -> fallback to CPU -> p99 spike. mitigations: route-level cache/control + allocator tuning + kv eviction.

sasha_support: great work :clap: — closing thread when we have the postmortem JSON to attach."
